caption: The drawing depicts a rounded, brown earthenware vessel with a single spout on its upper front side and an open circular mouth at the top. Attached to the vessel, there is a thick, braided handle in a darker shade of brown, which arches above the opening and is fastened to two small projections on either side of the vessel’s rim. The body of the vessel features inscriptions, including the name "John Austin" and the year "1847," both etched or carved into the surface. Above the inscription is a laurel or leaf motif positioned beneath the spout, and on the front surface below the inscription are two fish motifs, one directly beneath the year and another faintly outlined near the lower part of the body. The entire object is rendered with detailed shading to create a glossy, reflective appearance typical of glazed pottery. The background of the drawing is plain, off-white or beige, with a faint rectangular border framing the image.
title: Jug for Batter
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
